faqs.q: What happens during a preventive dental check-up?
faqs.a: A preventive check-up usually includes an examination of your teeth, gums and mouth, a professional cleaning to remove plaque and tartar, and X-rays when needed. Your dentist may also suggest fluoride treatment or sealants and give you advice on brushing, flossing and diet.

faqs.q: How often should I get my teeth professionally cleaned?
faqs.a: Most people are advised to have a professional cleaning and check-up about twice a year. If you have gum disease, smoke, have diabetes or build up tartar quickly, your dentist may recommend more frequent cleanings based on the condition of your teeth and gums.

faqs.q: Does scaling weaken or loosen teeth?
faqs.a: No, professional scaling by a dentist removes hardened tartar and does not weaken or loosen healthy teeth. Some people notice temporary sensitivity or small gaps afterwards, because the tartar that was covering the gums or filling those spaces has been removed, and this usually settles as the gums heal.

faqs.q: Are dental sealants useful for children?
faqs.a: Yes, sealants are thin protective coatings applied to the chewing surfaces of back teeth, where deep grooves easily trap food and bacteria. They are most often recommended for children once their permanent back teeth come through, though some adults also benefit, so ask your dentist whether they are suitable.
